## Version 2026.7.1

This release primarily focuses on type-safety, adding type annotations across
most of the built-in apps. Strong typing helps catch obscure code errors and also helps agents
more confidently edit and check code and will continue to be a priority in Pegasus.

While the changes touch a lot of files, they are almost entirely type annotations,
so upgrading should be relatively low-risk.

- **Added type annotations throughout the built-in apps** (teams, subscriptions, ecommerce, users,
  ai chat, dashboard, content, web, and the example apps).
  This is a continuation of the ongoing effort to improve the type safety of the codebase.
- Added a new `get_authenticated_user` helper to `apps.users.helpers`.
  It returns a properly-typed `CustomUser` for requests that are guaranteed to be authenticated,
  resolving API-key authentication when enabled. The DRF views and permission classes now use it.
  - **Upgrade Note**: This replaces `get_user_from_request` from `apps.api.helpers`, which has been removed.
    If you were using it, switch to the new helper.
- Documented the project's type annotation conventions in the AI rules files, including
  when to annotate `request` in views and when to use `get_authenticated_user`.
- Render deploys now wait for CI checks to pass. The `render.yaml` blueprint sets
  `autoDeployTrigger: checksPass` (when CI is enabled), so broken commits are no longer
  auto-deployed before your test suite finishes. Thanks Jacob for the suggestion!
- Added tests for the team model's helper properties and methods.
